description: Let Family Pulse present cleaner, household-meaningful merchant names than the raw synced feed by supporting per-transaction display-name overrides and optional exact-match rename rules for future synced transactions. The app keeps Plaid's raw fields intact while becoming easier to scan, search, and trust over time.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 2 transaction browser exists. Feature 21 is the preferred predecessor because the same transaction detail surface can host identity editing.

principles: Raw synced merchant/name fields are preserved exactly as received from Plaid or import sources
Display identity is a local Family Pulse layer that can be changed without corrupting sync provenance
Rename rules are optional; one-off cleanup must be possible without creating future behavior
V1 rule matching is exact on the raw synced source string — simple, predictable, reviewable
Checks are a special case: the UI should discourage automatic rule creation for 'Check ####' patterns
Current transaction edit and future rule creation are related but distinct actions
Applied identity rules should improve browsing/search without hiding original synced text from the detail view
Parent-only writes, kid-readable where the transaction itself is visible
SECRETS INVARIANT: identity overrides add household-friendly labels only, never expose raw Plaid payloads beyond already-visible merchant/name fields

techStack.database: PostgreSQL — transaction-level display override fields and a new merchant rename rules table
techStack.integrationPoints: Transaction list queries, sync upsert path, Monarch import path, and transaction detail UI
techStack.testing: node:test for exact-match rule application and API behavior; Playwright for transaction edit UX

userStories.title: Transaction-level display name override
acceptanceCriteria: A parent can edit the display merchant/payee name for a single transaction without changing the raw synced merchant_name or name columns
GET /api/transactions returns both raw displayable source text and the effective display name used in the UI
Transaction detail shows the original synced name and the local override when present
Clearing the override reverts the transaction to raw synced display text
Kid reads are allowed only when the transaction itself is visible to that kid; writes remain parent-only
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for set/clear behavior, response shape, auth guards, and preservation of raw source columns.

userStories.title: Optional exact-match future rename rules
acceptanceCriteria: When editing a transaction display name, parent can optionally create a future rename rule bound to the exact raw synced source string for that transaction
Rule matching in v1 is exact string match only against the raw synced source text chosen by the system
Creating a rule updates the current transaction display name and persists a rule for future synced transactions
Rules can be deleted or disabled later without altering the preserved raw source text on transactions
V1 does not require retroactively rewriting past matching transactions unless they are individually edited
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for exact-match rule creation, persistence, disabling, and non-retroactive behavior.

userStories.title: Check-aware default behavior
acceptanceCriteria: If the raw synced source text matches a check-style pattern such as 'Check 1024' or 'Check #1024', the UI defaults the 'apply to future matches' option to off
A one-off rename remains fully allowed for check transactions
Non-check transactions default the future-rule option to on for parent convenience
The heuristic is transparent and conservative; false positives are acceptable if the edit can still be changed
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for check-pattern detection helper plus UI-state assertion in Playwright or frontend unit-style coverage.

userStories.title: Rule application during sync and import
acceptanceCriteria: Plaid sync upsert path applies any exact-match rename rule to the transaction's effective display name during insert/update
Monarch import path can also apply rename rules when raw source text matches exactly
Rule application is idempotent across repeated syncs
If no rule matches, effective display name falls back to existing override or raw merchant/name
Raw synced source fields remain queryable and unchanged
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for sync/import application path with exact matches, misses, and repeated upserts.

userStories.title: Search and browsing use the effective display name
acceptanceCriteria: Transactions list and detail views render the effective display name prominently
Search can find matches by effective display name while still preserving discoverability of the raw synced text
API response includes enough fields for the browser to surface 'renamed from ...' context in detail view
Category rule creation remains based on deliberate product choice and is not silently changed by rename rules in v1
userStories.testStrategy: node:test for search behavior and response shape. Manual verification that renamed items are easier to scan in the list.

userStories.title: Rename rule management surface
acceptanceCriteria: Parents can list rename rules with raw source text, display name, enabled/disabled status, created_at, and last matched at
Parents can disable/delete a rule without affecting already renamed one-off transactions
V1 management can live in Settings or a simple modal/list; it does not require a large dedicated page
Auth guard is parent-only
userStories.testStrategy: node:test API coverage for list/update/delete plus manual UI check for rule visibility and controls.

high: If rename rules overwrite raw synced columns, provenance is lost. Mitigation: store effective display layer separately from merchant_name/name.
medium: Exact-match rules may miss real-world variants from Plaid. Mitigation: keep v1 exact and simple, then revisit normalized matching only if lived experience shows pain.
Mixing rename rules with category rules could create confusing behavior. Mitigation: keep them fully separate in data model and UI copy.

Clearing a display override while an exact-match rename rule still exists will let the next sync/import re-apply the rule. Mitigation: accept this as a v1 tradeoff until override provenance is tracked.
low: Search semantics may briefly feel surprising if both raw and effective names are searchable. Mitigation: show original name in detail so the mapping is obvious.

Deleting a rename rule does not clear display_name_override on already-renamed transactions because v1 does not track whether an override came from a rule or a manual edit. Mitigation: add override provenance if a future cascade-clear option becomes important.
operational: Future schema/design may want normalized matching. Mitigation: model rules so match_type can be extended later even if v1 only uses exact.

preFlightChecklist: Decide the exact raw source text hierarchy for rules: merchant_name first, fallback to name when merchant_name is absent
Confirm whether transaction list search should match both effective and raw names in the same query

Choose whether rule management belongs in transaction detail only or also a lightweight Settings list
